key_insight: PING embeds advection–diffusion physics in a graph neural network to forecast transport on irregular sensor networks and support solar power forecasting.
engineering_relevance: Improved cloud-motion forecasts can support intra-day photovoltaic power prediction and grid integration rather than directly optimize solar cells.
method: Represent advection–diffusion particle concentrations as graph signals.
Use a discretized advection–diffusion equation as a soft constraint in the training loss.
Couple PING with PV forecasting models using ground-sensor data and satellite cloud information.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports performance on par with state-of-the-art models on synthetic transport, sea surface temperature, and cloud-index datasets, plus improved intra-day PV forecasting through model coupling.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical gains or deployment costs, so operational benefits require validation on the target sensor network.
paper_title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
